item.title: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is low. Here's why you should care
item.description: The U.S. has tapped into its strategic oil reserve to help drive down rising gasoline prices in the wake of the war with Iran. Can oil from Venezuela help fill it back up?

item.title: American farmers are hurting -- and worried about their futures
item.description: Farmers who grow soybeans, corn, cotton and other crops are facing another year of losses as soaring fuel and fertilizer costs offset higher revenues.

item.title: How stores choose what to put on their shelves — like, say, Planet Money's board game
item.description: The most coveted real estate in business might just be the choicest shelf space of national big box retail. We go inside the room and the process of how stores choose what you can and can't buy.

item.title: The economic squeeze is pushing up poverty rates for older adults
item.description: Despite lower poverty overall, the rate for seniors has been steadily rising in recent years. A new AARP survey sheds light on how those over 50 are struggling in the crucial time before retirement.

item.title: eBay bans airbag sales as concerns about faulty or counterfeit parts rise
item.description: eBay became the latest online retailer to ban the sale of airbags and many of their components. Aftermarket parts can be risky if they turn out to be fake or defective.

item.title: Journalists for CNN, MS NOW and Politico return to the White House upon judge's orders
item.description: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration on Thursday to temporarily restore access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico, after they were banned from covering White House events by President Trump.

item.title: Will the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger be Hollywood's undoing?
item.description: Now that Paramount has an antitrust suit, the way is clear for a merger. But many say the deal will be the unmaking of Hollywood. NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with screenwriter and showrunner Mike Schur.

item.title: It's getting harder to afford rent in the U.S., even for middle-income families
item.description: Housing affordability challenges are spreading to higher income brackets, according to new research, which found one in five renters struggled last year to pay for their housing in full and on time.
